question.problem:
Find $\text{E}[{e}^{2X}],$ given that the continuous random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{{e}^{x}}{e-1},\,0\le x\le 1.
$$
question.worked_solution:
For a continuous random variable $X$ and a function $r(x),$ the rule of the lazy statistician states that 

$$
\text{E}[r(X)]={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
r(x)={e}^{2x}.
$$

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{e}^{2X}] & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }r(x)f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{e}^{2x}\cdot \frac{{e}^{x}}{e-1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{e}^{3x}}{e-1}\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{1}{3(e-1)}{e}^{3x}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{3(e-1)}{e}^{3}-\frac{1}{3(e-1)} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{3}-1}{3(e-1)}.\end{aligned}
$$
